about.title: Blythe Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Blythe sits along a major stretch of Interstate 10, and with that comes heavy commercial traffic, agricultural equipment, and consumer goods moving through and around the city daily. When a vehicle part fails, a piece of farm or industrial equipment malfunctions, or a household product turns out to be unsafe, the harm can be severe and sudden. Riverside County residents in Blythe who are hurt this way often face confusing questions about who is responsible — the manufacturer, a distributor, or a local retailer. California law gives injured people a path forward that doesn't require proving anyone was careless, only that a product was defective and that the defect caused harm. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we can put you in touch with an independent attorney who can review what happened, help you understand your options, and explain next steps without pressure or cost to speak with them.

whyChoose.title: Why Blythe Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: California generally allows product liability claims to proceed under strict liability, meaning you may not have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law, which matters when equipment or goods move through several hands before reaching a Blythe resident.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An independent attorney can advise you early on to preserve the product itself, since physical evidence often plays a central role in showing a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law often applies strict liability, so you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone acted negligently. An attorney can help evaluate the specific facts of your situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including packaging, instructions, or any broken pieces. Physical evidence is often important in defective product cases, and an attorney can advise you on how to preserve it properly.

items.question: I was hurt near I-10 in Blythe by a part that failed on my vehicle — does that count as product liability?
items.answer: It can, depending on the facts. If a vehicle part failure caused or contributed to your injury, it may involve both a product liability claim and a separate crash claim. A free connection through LawProactive can help you get in touch with an attorney who can sort out which claims may apply.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys, and those attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
